summary: Expose safe cleanup of unused Core-private backup credential handoffs through the existing support list and retire contract. API impact: changed existing contract; no new endpoint.

guide.reason: The currently supported NFS workflow uses no backup credential; unused-credential cleanup is an administrator support API, with no Controller UI flow.

api.reason: The existing Core report now includes redacted backup receipts and existing credential retire command can clear a safe unused backup receipt. Controller list/retire routes and payloads are unchanged. Core checks repository, unresolved operation and in-flight preparation references when listing and again when retiring; it retains a signed replay tombstone.

roadmap.reason: Closes a credential lifecycle gap in the existing destination candidate.

state.record: HMAC-protected private backup credential receipt on the pool master, cleared to a retained replay tombstone after an unused receipt is retired. A fresh Controller reads redacted receipt eligibility through Core report inventory.
state.reason: Controller holds no durable credential or cleanup registry. Member copies needed for later adoption are outside this master-only cleanup path.

verification.method: Focused Core receipt, failure, pending, in-flight, SMB file and ordinary-storage path tests plus focused race, privacy and diff checks passed. Independent read-only source review found no confirmed issue after tracing member adoption. On a disposable current-source capability overlay, the installed systemd Core executable digest was verified on both live hosts, four old failed handoffs appeared eligible and retired serially through Controller, replay left their empty-secret Core tombstones intact, five active receipts stayed ineligible, and four-kind access plus exact repository/point/run ID sets passed. All fixture processes stopped with the former master fenced. Forge CI is open.
verification.limits: No red baseline was captured before the fix. The four failed handoffs were originally made on an older binary, then retired on the matched current build. Exact credential POST replay timed out with HTTP 503; a subsequent Core report and private tombstone inspection confirmed no secret recreation. Active receipts were observed as ineligible, without an attempted active-retire command. Credential rotation, arbitrary interrupted retirement and forge CI remain open.
